protocolMetadata.instructions:
Sequence:

1. `tool_use`: `ask_firm_memory(question=<complete user message>)`
2. If the result contains `job:<uuid>`, do not return that interim receipt.
   Wait for the stated interval, or 30 seconds by default, then call
   `fetch(id="job:<uuid>")`. Keep polling while the job is queued, pending, or
   running.
3. Decide from the returned content whether it is a deterministic answer or a
   qualitative evidence packet.
   - A result containing the marker `firm-memory-mode: financial-authority` is
     the final answer from the controlling holdings ledger. Return the Markdown
     below the marker verbatim. Do not broaden or narrow the requested cohort,
     reclassify a returned row, recompute a total or subtotal, or add or omit a
     holding. Preserve its definitions, missingness, dates, and citations.
   - Deterministic fund/company metrics, complete enumerations, and job results
     are canonical. Preserve every number, cohort definition, source, as-of date,
     and `[Unclear]`; do not recompute them.
   - A result containing the marker `firm-memory-mode: qualitative-evidence` gives you
     governed source material, not a prewritten answer. Use your normal reasoning
     to answer the partner's original question directly, keep the response concise,
     and cite the sources you rely on. For a topic-discussion packet, lead with the
     general mechanisms, themes, and changes in the discussion; use named companies
     only as supporting examples. For other qualitative packets, lead with the most
     relevant current event. Do not reproduce the packet or unrelated company history.
   - For a broad topic-discussion packet, treat concrete mechanisms or adjacent concepts
     surfaced in the first packet as retrieval vocabulary, not as a company outline. If at
     least one material concept was absent from the partner's wording, make exactly one
     additional `ask_firm_memory` call phrased naturally around up to three such concepts,
     then synthesize both

tool.name: ask_firm_memory
tool.title: Ask Inspired's firm memory
tool.description:
Retrieve governed evidence or a canonical deterministic answer for an Inspired Capital question. Set `question` to the complete user message. Preserve exact numbers, cohorts, source links, dates, and `[Unclear]` in deterministic results. A `firm-memory-mode: financial-authority` result is final Markdown from the controlling holdings ledger. Return it verbatim without broadening, narrowing, reclassifying, recomputing, adding, or omitting any row or subtotal. When the result is marked `firm-memory-mode: qualitative-evidence`, use it as source material and answer the original question in your own concise prose; do not reproduce irrelevant packet sections. An interim `job:<uuid>` receipt must be resolved with fetch before answering.

Query Inspired Capital's institutional memory (portfolio companies, pipeline entities, prior partner discussions, memos, meeting notes, email threads).

INVOKE when the user asks about a known Inspired portfolio company, a pipeline entity Luke is tracking, prior partner discussions, portfolio-founder work history, attributed reading highlights, or a firm-internal topic. Examples: 'what did we say about Solace?', 'have we seen anything like Summer Health?', 'similar pass reasons around team scaling', 'what's our relationship with Aleph?', 'where is X today?', 'what have we highlighted about AI agents?', 'search our Readwise highlights for vertical software', 'which portco founders worked at Stripe?', 'do any of our portco founders have Meta Ads experience?', 'where is ShopMy's cap table?', 'how many companies are in our portfolio?', 'PortCo Smash rankings', 'which active Fund II companies are growing revenue fastest?', or a pasted forwarded email thread. Firm-memory owns fund membership and active/current portfolio categorization. Do not rebuild those cohorts in the host from a separate connector. For 'summarize the deck / data room / spreadsheet they just sent', the dedicated read_email_attachments tool is preferred (reads the files live), but this router also handles it the same way: it returns a `job:<uuid>`; call `fetch(id="job:<uuid>")` after the stated retry interval, or after 30 seconds by default, for up to five minutes. If metadata proves the attachment exists but it cannot be read, say so and ask the partner to upload it. Never infer its contents.

ASYNC RESULT CONTRACT: investment-to-now company evolution and larger finite named-company analyses may also return a `job:<uuid>` interim receipt so the request stays inside Cowork's host budget. Do not present that receipt as the answer and do not end the turn. Call `fetch(id="job:<uuid>")` after the stated interval, or after 30 seconds by default, and keep polling while the job is queued, pending, or running. Return only the final completed Markdown from fetch, preserving every heading, table, source link, and line break.

DO NOT INVOKE for general-knowledge questions about external companies Inspired hasn't engaged with (e.g., 'tell me about Brex/Stripe/Plaid' when those aren't portcos or pipeline). Answer those from your general knowledge and end with: 'Want me to check firm-memory for any Inspired context on X?'.

FAST-BAIL CONTRACT: the tool runs a sub-100ms probe before the heavy retrieval stack. If the target entity has no substantive context after alias-expanded entity matching, the tool returns `## Answer` with `[Unclear]`. Preserve that firm-specific gap. You may then add a separately labeled general-knowledge section for the unsupported clause, without presenting it as Inspired memory or altering any firm-memory facts.

For qualitative evidence packets, answer the partner's actual question and cite the relied-on sources. If two unrelated current situations are comparably plausible, ask one short follow-up question. For deterministic calculations and complete enumerations, preserve the returned facts and citations exactly. For multi-company pipeline meeting/email prep where the user names the companies, use pipeline_email_meeting_prep instead.

tool.name: read_email_attachments
tool.title: Read emailed attachments / data-room files live
tool.description:
Read the LIVE contents of files attached to an email or data room (deck, spreadsheet, financial model, memo). Downloads and extracts the text on demand — NOT the cached / ingested copy, so the financials are current.

INVOKE when the partner asks to 'summarize / read / open the deck / spreadsheet / data room / files they just sent / emailed / forwarded' or 'what are the key metrics in the attachment'. The reader is identity-scoped. It can read Luke's reporting mail, messages sent to pipeline@ / portfolio@ for any authenticated partner, or the caller's own mailbox when an exact caller-specific Gmail token is configured. Also try the partner's native Gmail / Drive connector for mail sent only to them.

Pass a Gmail search string: a company name ('Kalepa data room'), `from:sender`, `subject:deck`, etc. Returns a `job:<uuid>` handle immediately, then you MUST call `fetch(id="job:<uuid>")` to get the extracted text (file names, deck/spreadsheet/memo text, thread link). If `fetch` says still extracting, wait for the stated retry interval, or 30 seconds when none is stated, and poll for up to five minutes. Output returned markdown verbatim. If attachment metadata proves a file exists but the contents cannot be read, explicitly say the file was detected but not read and ask the partner to upload it. Never infer attachment contents.

tool.name: finalize_source_reconciliation
tool.title: Finalize a named-source reconciliation
tool.description: Fail-closed finalizer for a comparison between a named pitch and an internal technical discussion, with an optional white paper only when the question asks for it. Call only after independently reading every requested document and retrieving the identity-bound internal discussion. Attempt those retrievals FIRST, before asking the user anything: run the document reads and the internal-discussion query immediately. Never ask where a document lives, whether it exists, or which company is meant until every retrieval attempt has reached a terminal state; a clarification request without an attempted retrieval is an error. When sources remain missing after the attempts, call this tool anyway and return its bounded partial statuses verbatim. Pass each complete connector result verbatim. The tool derives the four exact statuses read, partial_read, detected_not_read, and not_found. It withholds the claim matrix unless every requested source is read and every comparison row contains an exact source-local quote plus a URL present in that source result. Output the returned Markdown verbatim.

tool.name: capture_meeting_to_affinity
tool.title: Capture a verified founder-company meeting in Affinity
tool.description: Capture a completed meeting with a non-portfolio founder only after list_post_pitch_capture_candidates verifies the canonical Granola source in the exact Inspired Capital team Pitches folder. The server rechecks explicit firm-shared source access, folder membership, fresh source evidence, and authenticated caller identity before any Affinity access. The caller need not have attended. Never add the executing caller to meeting attendees or owner selection merely because it runs the service. A formal pitch or fundraising label is not required. The write is idempotent by source and calendar event. Set first_pitch_verified only for a positive introductory founder conversation. Every eligible meeting ensures one Deals entry, including follow-ups. The core checks exact company identity and fresh native Deals membership before creation. Reuse existing entries and preserve every existing owner, including blanks. Only two existing Status transitions are permitted: To Reach Out to First Meeting, and First Meeting to 2+ M'tgs & Diligence after a verified prior distinct pitch. All other statuses and deal fields stay unchanged. For any newly created entry the core derives owners from known Granola named participants, without additional transcript proof for ownership. Partners take priority over Luke/Lex, who may own only when solo. Multiple partners use the participating meeting scheduler, verified from canonical calendar creator/organizer evidence. Unknown or conflicting scheduler evidence leaves ownership unresolved. Mailing-list expansion does not establish participation. owner_email is only a legacy hint and may be omitted. Read the complete owner set from the returned owner_emails and owner_ids. Pass founder_company_meeting_verified, founder_present_verified, meeting_completed_verified, and verified company-domain evidence. Set prior_pitch_verified only when a separate prior completed pitch is established. Never infer first-pitch or prior-pitch evidence from a missing record. Use dry_run=true for setup and smoke tests. repair_missing_deal_entry=true is only for an explicit user request to repair a missing Deals entry on this exact successful note capture, including a follow-up. It preserves the note, repeats every creation check, and never changes existing owners. Repair mode may also reconcile a verified missing-entry coverage incident. Never blindly retry an uncertain repair. New entries use First Meeting unless a distinct prior founder-company meeting is verified, then 2+ M'tgs & Diligence. repair_owner_assignment=true is Luke-only explicit correction of an exact workflow-created owner assignment. It requires unchanged native owners matching the original audit, the unchanged full note, and current canonical source/company/portfolio proof. It changes only Owners and never replays the note.

result.displayName: Capture a verified founder-company meeting in Affinity

tool.name: submit_firm_memory_smoke_report
tool.title: Archive a partner-device smoke report
tool.description: Store one complete privacy-safe firm-memory smoke artifact in the dedicated QA archive. Invoke exactly once after the smoke report and parity ledger are frozen. The authenticated caller is derived from the MCP session. The tool never accepts a caller override, never writes sources or mentions, and never makes the report answer evidence. Pass the minimal rule-53 REFERENCE_PACKET or COMPARISON_RESULT archive projection, not the complete in-session report. Only a Luke REFERENCE may include verbatim raw output for SHARED_EXACT records. Every COMPARISON record, including SHARED_EXACT, must use the strict redacted functional envelope and the fixed shared_exact_fields hash map. The server resolves the archived Luke reference and enforces its probe inventory, parity classes, and hashes before accepting a passing grade. Never include the device-local private appendix or comparison raw output. Reusing the same run ID with the same bytes is idempotent. Reusing it with different bytes is rejected. Use dry_run=true only during partner setup validation.

tool.title: Fund / company position facts
tool.description: Deterministic, cited, source-of-truth lookup for Inspired fund financials — for ONE fund OR ALL funds at once. A `firm-memory-mode: financial-authority` result is final: return its Markdown verbatim and do not reclassify or omit holdings.

_published_faq.name: How do I add firm-memory to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add firm-memory to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor by connecting its remote MCP URL in each client's MCP settings. In Claude, add a custom connector. In ChatGPT, add an MCP app. In Cursor, add an MCP server under Settings. The MCP URL is https://firm-memory-mcp.fly.dev/mcp.

_published_faq.name: Is firm-memory MCP ready for ChatGPT and Claude?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 14, 2026, firm-memory scores 96/100 on Manufact's MCP publishing checklist. The scan meets ChatGPT publishing checks and meets Claude publishing checks. Passing these checks does not guarantee marketplace approval.

_published_faq.name: How clear is firm-memory's MCP tool documentation?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 14, 2026, firm-memory scores 63/100 in Manufact's review of tool titles, descriptions, input and output schemas, and behavior annotations. The review covers 31 of 31 discovered tools. The quality score measures documentation clarity; runtime behavior and marketplace readiness require separate checks.

_published_faq.name: What are the best alternatives to firm-memory?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 17, 2026, alternatives to firm-memory in financial-services on the Manufact MCP catalog include Contract-Factory — Sociétés & SIREN, Kavara Kirk, CeylonCharts, Netzo, and Ramp Data.
